meta.description: Assignment of cause/effect (eitza) nodes to existing bechina-based packages for Torah #221

assignments.reason: Tithing (מעשר) is the holy practice that activates the Great Hand and produces contentment. In this Torah, the Rebbe explicitly teaches that 'through maaser one achieves the aspect of contentment, which is the aspect of the Great Hand.' Its essential nature — a mitzvah of giving that generates divine sufficiency — places it squarely within the domain of Package 1 (divine provision and contentment). It is the human-action face of the same reality that Package 1 describes from the divine side.

The act of giving tithe (נותנין מעשר) is functionally identical to מעשר in essential nature — both refer to the mitzvah of tithing. It is the initiating cause in the summary edge (id=2179) that leads to salvation from enemies. Same domain as Package 1: the practice that activates divine provision.

assignments.node_id: השם יתברך מושיט ידו ומכסה עליו ונצול משונאים
assignments.node_text: הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מוֹשִׁיט יָדוֹ וּמְכַסֶּה עָלָיו וְנִצּוֹל מִשּׂוֹנְאִים
assignments.reason: God extending His hand and covering/protecting the person is the Great Hand (יד הגדולה) in action — the direct manifestation of Package 1's dominant node. The essential nature of this concept is divine protection through God's hand, which is precisely the 'Great Hand' that defines Package 1. The verse 'וּבְצֵל יָדִי כִּסִּיתִיךָ' (in the shadow of My hand I have covered you) makes the identity explicit: the covering hand IS the Great Hand.

Being saved from enemies is the ultimate outcome of the Great Hand's protection. Its essential nature is salvation/divine rescue — the result of God covering the person with His hand. In this Torah, rescue from enemies is inseparable from the Great Hand's action: the entire teaching builds toward showing that the Great Hand saves. This places it within Package 1's domain of divine provision and protection.
